data.G: Keep the supplied src/candidate.cpp unchanged as the initial G. After research, integrate only measured candidates and independently confirm the integrated program for correctness and wall-clock performance.
data.analysis: Choose N=3: the source exposes three complementary opportunities—serial execution despite a threads argument, a scalar-looking contiguous-x stencil kernel, and six dependent timesteps that may benefit from cache/temporal blocking. The supplied automatic baseline is correct; its three timings are 0.472935, 0.464826, and 0.456954 seconds (mean 0.464905 seconds). No separate one- versus four-core baseline timings are supplied, so require each tree to measure both budgets and do not infer per-core speedups. All candidates must modify only src/candidate.cpp, preserve full initialization, boundaries, both output buffers, generic valid n, and the stated tolerance. Three tracks are sufficient; initialization is semantically specified and already uses bulk operations, so it is not a separate research objective.

children.objective: Replace the serial timestep sweeps with OpenMP parallel work over disjoint rows or slabs, honoring the run-time threads argument as the CPU budget. Preserve a synchronization point between timesteps before buffer roles change, and retain the exact update domain, full initialization, and boundary values. Measure one- and four-thread wall time, including initialization and any parallel-region overhead; validate all supplied correctness checks.
children.subject: Honor the thread budget with timestep-synchronized OpenMP parallelism

children.objective: Make the contiguous-x radius-3 update easier to vectorize, for example through row-pointer addressing and a clean vectorizable inner loop. Do not assume row alignment from the 64-byte base alignment; handle tails and generic n. Use only vector features supported by the actual build target, preserve the recurrence and boundaries, and check the fixed numerical tolerance. Measure one- and four-thread performance.
children.subject: Vectorize the radius-3 stencil kernel along x

children.objective: Explore cache blocking or halo-aware space-time tiling for the six dependent timesteps to improve local data reuse. Account for the radius-three dependency at each step and ensure the returned even and odd buffers, including boundaries, match the baseline; retain its full initialization semantics. Include scratch allocation and all work in timing, avoid benchmark-size specialization, and compare correctness and wall time at both thread budgets.
children.subject: Improve six-step cache reuse with spatial or temporal tiling
